{ "item": { "id": "5d4595b3-af60-41b2-85ae-c325cd927db2", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Glossary", "short_description": "Definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.", "body": "

Glossary

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Rate limits & errors.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.
", "version_token": "7ab1a9d9-5794-4b46-abe4-107b2ce6b983", "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:18:16.350Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-20T15:07:12.033Z", "placement_id": "95ce79ad-46ed-430e-b002-4050b41ad408", "folder_id": "08088d6d-fe4a-4704-b265-9636d2cd750e", "file_name": "glossary" } }

{ "item": { "id": "e877d6e3-b7f3-4929-863d-4b4b7171147d", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Concepts", "short_description": "The three core building blocks of Godzilla: pipelines, connectors, and events.", "body": "{{ds:component/hero|title=Concepts|subtitle=The three building blocks every Godzilla pipeline is made of.|cta_html=Start with Pipelines}}

Godzilla is built from three ideas that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/5ac66235-69dc-4092-b430-9d68837e0c76}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/7418c3d6-9ea1-4d1c-8d8f-73136f6b6abb}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/6277e4fb-3e99-45b0-a7f6-aefe69c5778f}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}}

Declaring and validating event structures

Once you understand pipelines, connectors, and events, the next step is learning how to formally declare what your event payloads look like and validate them in flight.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/f2e5fa8f-30dc-4d9b-8c88-15cc24fadec4}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=JSON Schema declarations and validation rules to ensure event payload integrity across your pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

To ensure data quality, you can attach schemas to validate event payloads at the pipeline input or at transform boundaries.

input.body:
{{ds:component/hero|title=Concepts|subtitle=The three building blocks every Godzilla pipeline is made of.|cta_html=Start with Pipelines}}

Godzilla is built from three ideas that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/ed0d065b-2d21-448c-b921-9966af9c5dc4}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/656ae370-0023-4069-b23a-04a922bc2181}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}} {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/b96ee14b-2fce-4956-91d9-e9d8a596efd7}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}}

Declaring and validating event structures

Once you understand pipelines, connectors, and events, the next step is learning how to formally declare what your event payloads look like and validate them in flight.

{{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/f2e5fa8f-30dc-4d9b-8c88-15cc24fadec4}}|tag=Concept|title=Schemas|description=JSON Schema declarations and validation rules to ensure event payload integrity across your pipelines.}}

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

To ensure data quality, you can attach schemas to validate event payloads at the pipeline input or at transform boundaries.

Definitions

Quick reference definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Error handling & recovery.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Limits, quotas & errors.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.
